facts.content: The assessment is dermatitis, likely irritant or contact dermatitis related to occupational exposure to housekeeping cleaning agents, with palmar involvement and chronicity of approximately 3 to 4 months.
facts.source_text: 1) Dermatitis, likely irritant/contact dermatitis related to occupational exposure (housekeeping cleaning agents) with palmar involvement; chronicity ~3–4 months;

facts.content: Symptoms contributing to the assessment include dryness, cracking, itching, and occasional bleeding related to scratching.
facts.source_text: symptoms include dryness, cracking, itching, occasional scratching-related bleeding.

facts.content: Patient is advised to avoid or identify triggers and to wear gloves at all times during cleaning and review products used at work.

facts.content: A topical corticosteroid cream and regular emollients are recommended for the affected hands, to be applied three to four times daily.
facts.source_text: Therapeutics: topical corticosteroid cream for inflammation + regular emollients; apply to affected hands 3–4 times daily.

facts.content: A prescription for a topical corticosteroid cream and a moisturizing emollient will be sent to the pharmacy.

facts.content: Patient is educated to continue moisturizing, protect skin from irritants, and monitor for signs of infection or worsening.

facts.content: The patient should be reassessed in 10 to 14 days, or sooner if symptoms worsen or spread, and if there is no improvement, additional options will be considered.
